title: Moral Duty vs Epistemic Inference: Deber vs Deber de

sections.content:
You know *deber* + infinitive for obligation (*Debes llamar*) and *deber de* + infinitive for probability or inference (*Debe de estar en casa*, *Debe de haber salido*) from B2 Unit 26. In ethical analysis, this distinction carries sharp weight in the past and in general principles:

• **Past moral duty (*debió* / *debía* + infinitive, no *de*)**: states what a person was morally obliged to do (*Debió obrar con honestidad*; *Debía respetar la dignidad ajena*).
• **Past epistemic inference (*debió de* + infinitive / *debe de haber* + participle)**: draws a reasoned inference about someone's motive (*Debió de obrar por egoísmo*; *Debe de haber actuado por altruismo*).
• **Impersonal ethical norms (*se debe* + infinitive, no *de*)**: formulates universal duties (*Se debe proteger la integridad de toda persona*).

sections.title: Moral duty (no de) vs inference (de)
rows: Debió obrar con honestidad ante el grupo.
She ought to have acted with honesty before the group. (duty)
Debió de obrar por miedo a las críticas.
She must have acted out of fear of criticism. (inference)
Se debe respetar la dignidad de cada individuo.
One must respect the dignity of every individual. (norm)
Su silencio debe de responder a un cálculo práctico.
His silence must be due to a practical calculation. (inference)

items.spanish: Aunque la inferencia parezca lógica, no podemos afirmar que debió de actuar por egoísmo sin pruebas.
items.english: Although the inference may seem logical, we cannot claim that he must have acted out of egoism without evidence.

items.spanish: En aquel dilema, el representante debió obrar con integridad y explicar los riesgos reales.
items.english: In that dilemma, the representative had a duty to act with integrity and explain the real risks.

items.spanish: Se debe valorar el altruismo sin ignorar la honestidad de las intenciones.
items.english: One must value altruism without ignoring the honesty of intentions.

items.spanish: Quien guardó silencio debe de haber temido perder la confianza de sus colegas.
items.english: Whoever kept silent must have feared losing the trust of their colleagues.

sections.content: In formal Spanish, *deber de* + infinitive is reserved for inference/probability and is rejected by style guides for moral obligation: never write `*Se debe de respetar la dignidad*` when stating a duty. Keep *deber* (no *de*) for obligation and *deber de* for inference.
